cards.text: Saul, Israel’s king, has been hunting David day after day (1 Samuel 23:14), and David already spared him once, in a cave (1 Samuel 24). Now the Ziphites, people from around Ziph, show up at Saul’s place in Gibeah with a tip. Isn’t David hiding on the hill of Hachilah, opposite Jeshimon?

cards.question: The Ziphites tell Saul that David is hiding on the hill of Hachilah. Saul decides to stay home in Gibeah.

cards.text: Saul brings three thousand chosen men of Israel down to the Wilderness of Ziph and camps beside the road at Hachilah. Three THOUSAND men to find ONE guy on ONE hill!

cards.question: Out in the wilderness, David realizes Saul has followed him. David sends out spies to make sure Saul has really arrived.

cards.text: Most people run AWAY from three thousand soldiers, but David heads straight for the camp to take a look. He spots where Saul has lain down, along with Abner son of Ner, the general of Saul’s army.

cards.question: With three thousand troops in the camp, Saul himself is lying inside the ___ of the camp.

cards.text: David turns to Ahimelech the Hittite (not Ahimelech the priest) and Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother. He asks which of them will go down with him to Saul in the camp.

cards.question: David asks Ahimelech the Hittite and Abishai who will go down with him into Saul’s camp. Who says yes?

cards.text: That night David and Abishai come right up to the troops, and there’s Saul, asleep in the inner circle, with his spear stuck in the ground by his head. Abner and the troops are lying all around him, and David just… walks up.

cards.question: Abishai is standing over the sleeping king, with Saul’s own spear right there. What does Abishai want to do?

answers.text: Pin Saul to the ground with the spear
Tie Saul up and carry him off
Wake Saul up and make him surrender

cards.text: Abishai says, “Today God has delivered your enemy into your hand.” He wants to do it in one stroke, and he says he won’t need to strike Saul twice.

cards.question: Abishai is ready to strike. Why does David tell him not to destroy Saul?
David says Saul’s day will come and he’ll die, or he’ll go into battle and perish. Who does David say will strike Saul down?
David won’t let Abishai strike Saul. He tells Abishai to leave everything by Saul’s head untouched and just walk away.

cards.text: David says the LORD forbid that he should extend his hand against the LORD’s anointed. He tells Abishai to take the spear and water jug by Saul’s head, and then they’ll go.

cards.question: David and Abishai head out with the spear and water jug, and nobody in the camp wakes up. A deep ___ from the LORD has fallen on them.

cards.text: In and out with the king’s own spear and water jug, and no one saw them or knew about it. Three thousand men, and not ONE of them so much as rolled over.
David crosses to the other side and stands on top of the mountain at a distance. There’s a wide gulf between them.

cards.question: From across the gulf, the first one David shouts to is Saul himself.

cards.text: David shouts to the troops and to Abner, and Abner calls back, “Who are you who calls to the king?” Then David starts in on him: you’re a man, aren’t you, and who in Israel is your equal?

cards.question: David says nobody in Israel is Abner’s equal. So what does David want to know from Abner?

answers.text: Why he didn’t protect the king
Why he brought so many troops
Why he came into the wilderness

cards.text: David tells Abner this thing he has done is not good. As surely as the LORD lives, David says, all of them deserve to die, since they did not protect their lord, the LORD’s anointed.
Then comes the line I use every time my sprinkles go missing: “Now look around.” And David asks, “Where are the king’s spear and water jug that were by his head?”

cards.question: When David’s voice carries across the gulf, it’s Saul himself who recognizes it.
Saul calls out, “Is that your voice, David my son?” David says it is. Then what does David ask the king?

answers.text: Will you make me your general
Can I come back to Gibeah

cards.text: David keeps going: what has he done, and what evil is in his hand? If the LORD stirred Saul up against him, may He accept an offering, but if men did it, may they be cursed in the presence of the LORD.

cards.question: If men stirred Saul up, David says, they have driven him away today from sharing in the ___ of the LORD, telling him to go serve other gods.
David asks Saul not to let his blood fall far from the presence of the LORD. Then he says the king of Israel has come out, like someone hunting a partridge in the mountains, to look for what?
Saul hears David out and refuses to admit he’s done anything wrong.

cards.text: Saul answers, “I have sinned. Come back, David my son.” He says he’ll never harm David again, because today David considered his life precious.
Then Saul says, “I have played the fool and have committed a grave error!” Friend, I said almost that exact line the day I put in a whole batch and forgot the timer.

cards.question: David crosses back over the gulf to hand Saul his spear in person.

cards.text: “Here is the king’s spear,” David answers, and he tells Saul to let one of the young men come over and get it. He is NOT carrying it back across that gulf himself, and honestly, friend, neither would I.

Then David says, “May the LORD repay every man for his righteousness and faithfulness.” The LORD delivered Saul into his hand today, and for the SECOND time (1 Samuel 24), David would not extend his hand against the LORD’s anointed.

cards.question: David says he valued Saul’s life today. What does David ask the LORD to do with David’s own life?

answers.text: Value it and rescue him from trouble
Make it long and full of riches
Keep it hidden in the wilderness

cards.question: Saul tells David, “May you be blessed, David my son.” He says David will accomplish great things and will surely prevail. After that, where does each of them go?

answers.text: David leaves and Saul goes home

cards.text: Hang on to your apron, friend, because this story is still in the oven.
